title: The Locked Library
intro: You wake up on the cold floor of a locked library. Dust hangs in the lamplight. You can make out a **desk**, a **bookshelf**, a **painting**, a **locked drawer** and a heavy **door** with a four-digit keypad. Find a way out.

examine.text: A cluttered oak desk heaped with papers.

Floor-to-ceiling shelves of dusty volumes. Four books stand out of line with the rest: one red, one blue, one green and one black. Something is scratched on their spines, but you would need to look at the books themselves.
Through the magnifying glass you can read tiny handwritten numbers on the spines: the red book bears a 5, the blue book a 2, the green book a 9. The black book has only a smudge.
Tiny numbers are scratched on the spines, far too small to read with the naked eye. Something that magnifies might help.
The portrait's frame has swung open on a hidden hinge, revealing a hollow in the wall. The plaque still reads: 'Founder of the library, 1863'.
A stern portrait of a bearded man. A brass plaque reads: 'Founder of the library, 1863'. The frame has a tiny keyhole in its side.
A small drawer in the desk, locked with a three-digit dial. You could try entering a code.
The keypad glows faintly green, waiting for a four-digit code.
A heavy door with a four-digit keypad. The keypad is dark and unresponsive - it seems to have no power. Beneath it there is a small empty fuse slot.

magnifying_glass.name: magnifying glass
magnifying_glass.examine: A brass-rimmed magnifying glass. Good for reading tiny print.

old_note.name: old note
old_note.examine: Scrawled in a hurry: 'Red, blue, green - in that order. Ignore the black one.'

brass_key.name: brass key
brass_key.take_text: You take the small brass key.
brass_key.examine: A small brass key with a delicate, narrow bit.

fuse.name: fuse
fuse.take_text: You take the glass fuse from the hollow.
fuse.examine: A glass cartridge fuse, the kind used in old electrical panels.

use_rules.text: The key turns with a click and the portrait swings open like a door, revealing a hollow in the wall. Inside you see a small glass fuse and a slip of paper that reads: 'The founder's year opens the way out.'
You press the fuse into the slot beneath the keypad. The keypad flickers to life with a soft green glow.

use_rules.fail_text: The drawer has a dial, not a keyhole. The key does not fit.

drawer.wrong_text: The dial clicks into place but the drawer stays shut. That is not the right code.
drawer.success_text: The dial clicks and the drawer slides open. Inside lies a small brass key.

door.locked_text: The keypad is dark. Pressing the keys does nothing at all.
door.wrong_text: The keypad buzzes angrily and flashes red. Wrong code.
door.success_text: The keypad beeps, the bolt thunders back and the heavy door swings open onto fresh night air. You have escaped the Locked Library!

hints.text: Start with the desk - people hide things under papers.
There are useful objects on the desk. Take them.
Something about the bookshelf looks out of order.
The odd books carry writing too small to read. Something might magnify it.
The numbers on the books, read in the order the note gives, fit the drawer's three-digit dial.
Take what is inside the drawer.
The portrait's frame has a keyhole.
Something is hidden behind the portrait.
The door's keypad has no power. Look for a slot, and something that fits it.
A year is written somewhere in this room. Which one opens the way out?
